title: Rectangle Claim: Area
subject: math
goal: Make rectangles, find their area by counting and by rows times columns, and claim the most squares.
materials: a pencil or crayon for each player

roles.name: Leader
jobs: Make sure everyone gets a turn.

roles.name: Writer
jobs: Write each rectangle in the table.
say: How many rows? How many in each row?

roles.name: Checker
jobs: Check each area two ways: count, and rows times columns.

roles.name: Reporter
jobs: Tell the class what your group found.

steps: Take turns. Roll two dice. The two numbers are the sides of your rectangle.
Draw your rectangle on the grid, along the lines, anywhere it fits. Put your initial in it.
Count the squares inside. That's the area. Write it in your rectangle.
The Checker checks: rows times the number in each row. Does it match your count?
No room? Pass. After 4 rounds (everyone has had 4 turns), add up your areas. The most area wins.

table.title: Our rectangles (write your initial with each)

listen_for: Counting the lines instead of the squares.
Students noticing that 2 by 6 and 3 by 4 have the same area.
“The longer rectangle is bigger.” Ask the Checker to count both.
debrief: Ask: who made a rectangle with an area of 12? What sides did it have? Are there others?
Ask: is there a faster way than counting every square?
sources: The idea is also modeled in PhET Interactive Simulations' Area Builder (University of Colorado Boulder). The game and questions were written for Paper Loop.
